changelog.summary: Original shape: cases at the MonContext boundary (monNumber, argAddresses, initial/final {regs, ram}, kFlag, provenance, source, notes). No CALLG bytes, no MMU state.

Lifted cases to drive a real CALLG instruction through the indirect-segment-31 capability + program MMU decode path: added per-case 'mmu' and 'callg' blocks plus initial.regs.pc / final.regs.pc / final.regs.l. Rationale at the time: exercise the real dispatch boundary end-to-end on both emulators.

REVERTED to the v1.0.0 MonContext boundary shape (this decision settled on the C side - see 'caseBoundary' below for the full reasoning) - removed 'mmu'/'callg' blocks and pc/l register fields. ALSO corrected SINTRAN background-program error codes against Appendix A (several prior codes, e.g. decimal 41/52/57, were either drawn from the WRONG Appendix A table (RT-program namespace, not background-program) or invented outright with no source; see 'errorCodeCorrections' below). Status set to DRAFT / NOT FROZEN per explicit C-side request.

caseBoundary.boundary: MonContext (the interface nd500x's nd500_indirect.c hands to mon_dispatch() after intercepting a segment-31 CALLG and resolving the operand effective addresses).
caseBoundary.why: The C side settled this: ALL MON semantics - parameter layout, byte counts, error codes, 32-bit INTEGER width, file effects - live at or below the MonContext boundary. The two things that boundary does NOT exercise (CALLG operand decoding, MMU translation) are already covered elsewhere: CALLG operand decoding by nd500_tests.json (the general CPU instruction corpus), and MMU translation by test_mmu_translation. Lifting this shared spec to full CALLG byte encoding + MMU capability-table state (as v2.0.0 did) would force emulator-specific MMU state into language-neutral JSON for zero parity gain on MON semantics - the thing this spec exists to test.
notExercisedHere: CALLG operand decoding (opcode/operand-mode encoding, effective-address computation for CONSTANT/CONSTANT_SHORT/ABSOLUTE argument operands) - covered by nd500_tests.json.
MMU translation (program/data MMU enable, capability tables, page-index tables, PS_AZI/PS_ASI/PS_ADI page-status modes) - covered by test_mmu_translation.

contractPoints.flatIdentityRamMmuOff: Both harnesses build the MonContext directly (no CPU/CALLG step, no MMU translation layer engaged). 'argAddresses' in every case are therefore DIRECT offsets into the case's 'ram' array - flat, identity-mapped, MMU OFF. A runner MUST NOT apply any address translation to argAddresses or to any address embedded in 'ram'.
contractPoints.integerParamsAre32Bit: Every ND-500 INTEGER-typed MON parameter (per the YAML 'type: INTEGER' field) is a 32-BIT WORD, read/written via the equivalent of mon_read_param_word / mon_write_param_word - NEVER a 16-bit halfword. This applies uniformly across all 34 covered calls; a runner that reads/writes INTEGER parameters as 16-bit halfwords will mis-decode every case with more than one INTEGER parameter (the second parameter's address would be off by a factor of 2 from what 'argAddresses' expects).

callgConvention.dispatchBoundary: MON calls dispatch when a CALLG's resolved target capability has PC_IND set and targets SINTRAN segment 31 (see nd500x src/cpu/nd500_indirect.c nd500_check_indirect_call); the offset within segment 31 IS the MON number directly (not divided by 4).
callgConvention.argumentsAreAddresses: Per ND-05.009.4 EN section 13.7 (CALLG), each CALLG argument slot holds the EFFECTIVE ADDRESS of the parameter, not its value. Cases encode this as 'argAddresses': [...] mirroring MonContext.arg_addresses[].
callgConvention.errorConvention: On error, the error code is written to W1 (== I1 / I[0] on ND-500) and the K (skip/error) flag is set; caller code then does 'IF K GO ERROR'. This is stated in nearly every YAML's assembly_500 example ('ERROR: W1 =: ErrCode').
callgConvention.kFlagField: Each case has a top-level 'kFlag' boolean: expected K-flag state after mon_dispatch() returns.
callgConvention.registerModel: regs use 'i1'..'i4' (I[0..3]) plus 'st' (status word), matching the key names already used by test_instruction_validation.c's known_regs[] array in nd500x, so the harness's existing register read/write helpers can be reused verbatim.
callgConvention.rawStateModel: RESOLVED 2026-07-10 (was OPEN in schema v1.0.0): cases now drive a REAL CALLG instruction through the indirect-segment-31 capability + program MMU, not a MonContext shortcut. Verified by reading src/cpu/nd500_indirect.c (nd500_check_indirect_call), src/cpu/nd500_mmu.c/.h, and src/cpu/instructions/CALL/Callg.c on the C side, cross-checked against CpuND500.IndirectSegments.cs / CpuND500.MMU.cs / Instructions/CALL/Callg.cs on the C# side. cases.source: No manual (Appendix A) or call-specific YAML entry grounds a numeric error code for this condition; downgraded from an unverifiable literal value to K-flag-only per project honesty rule. mon-calls-described.md '## MON 321B - **NOT FOUND**': '321B UEADM  UEAdministrator / Handle Yser Environment / MON call no longer suported. / Return with K flag set' (verbatim from the described.md extraction of the manual text); exact numeric error value 52 confirmed by plan NC_TOOLCHAIN_MON_PLAN.md 'Known bugs to fix first': 'C MON 321B returns success; must return error 52 + K flag (deprecated), matching C# and the manual.'
cases.notes: No YAML file exists for 321B; description sourced entirely from mon-calls-described.md's manual-text extraction, not from a structured YAML. Return with K flag set' - no numeric error code is given anywhere in the source. The plan's prior claim ('must return error 52 + K flag') is one of the invented/unverified codes flagged for correction; only the K-flag-set behavior is manual-grounded.
